summary: Two work together behind. Three connect. One gives us a forward option.
sourceLabel: How We Play research draft based on England Football Learning 7v7 guidance and published grassroots coaching discussion (22 October 2026).
gives: two defenders learning to support each other
a central midfielder linking both ends
a striker who can offer depth or a short pass
shapeCue: A starting picture, not somewhere we have to stay. Let players try different roles.

status.source: How We Play researched draft, 22 October 2026. Qualified coaching review pending.

shape.title: Starting shape: 1-2-3-1
shape.caption: Two defenders, three midfielders and one striker, with a goalkeeper.
shape.altSummary: Seven players attack upwards: goalkeeper at the bottom; left defender 3 and right defender 2; left midfielder 11, central midfielder 8 and right midfielder 7; striker 9 highest. Positions illustrate a possible starting shape, not compulsory running lanes.

rules.title: Give two options
rules.tag: Help our goalkeeper start play without forcing a pass.
rules.summary: The two defenders spread out to offer clear passes; 8 can support ahead.
rules.cue: Can our keeper see two choices?
rules.extra: Look short when it is safe. If it isn't on, don't force it.
rules.src: How We Play research draft, 22 October 2026
look: 3 and 2 separate to offer the goalkeeper passing angles.
8 stays available ahead as a potential next pass, rather than hiding behind an opponent.
If no safe short pass is available, players aren't forced into one.

rules.title: Big with it, small without it
rules.tag: Use the width when we attack; get closer when we defend.
rules.summary: 11 and 7 stretch the pitch in possession and recover inside without it.
rules.cue: Ball ours? Wide. Ball theirs? Closer.
rules.extra: Starting positions help us; they're not painted lines on the pitch.
rules.seo: 7v7 width: wide in possession, connected in defence
rules.src: How We Play coaching synthesis; England Football community discussion, 22 October 2026
look: When we have the ball, the wide midfielders give their teammates room and an outside pass.
When the opposition have it, the wide midfielders move closer to 8 and help protect the middle.
The whole team responds to the ball; wide players aren't trapped in channels.

rules.title: One presses, one covers
rules.tag: When one defender meets the ball, the other protects the danger behind.
rules.summary: Two defenders work as a pair, not both chasing the same opponent.
rules.cue: If your mate goes, where do you cover?
rules.extra: Don't leave your partner defending the goal alone.
rules.seo: 7v7 defending pairs: pressing and covering in 2-3-1
rules.src: How We Play research draft, 22 October 2026
look: The closest defender chooses whether to meet the ball.
The other defender protects the route towards goal.
Our central midfielder helps close the space ahead rather than abandoning the centre.

rules.title: Lose it, find home
rules.summary: The closest player slows the attack while teammates recover to protect the middle.
rules.cue: Who slows them? Where do I help?
rules.extra: You don't all have to win the ball. Give the team time to get organised.
rules.seo: 7v7 defensive transition: lose it find home
rules.src: How We Play research draft, 22 October 2026
look: The nearest player slows the opposition if it's safe to do so.
Both wide midfielders recover to help the team get connected.
The defender pair protects the route to our goal.

roles.title: Goalkeeper
roles.head: Start us playing
points: Look for safe passing options to our two defenders.
Try a short pass when the picture is clear; do not force it if the pass is blocked.
Help the team with calm information when the other side has the ball.
roles.cue: Can I see two good choices?

roles.title: The two defenders
roles.head: Give options. Protect together.
points: With the ball, move apart enough to be seen by our goalkeeper.
When the opposition attack, work together: one can meet the danger, the other covers.
Stay close enough that you can help one another when possession changes.
roles.cue: If my partner goes, where should I be?

roles.title: Central midfielder
roles.head: Connect the team
points: Make yourself available for a pass between the defenders and striker.
Look for the wide players when they have room.
When we lose the ball, protect the space in front of our defenders.
roles.cue: Can I help the player on the ball?

roles.title: Wide midfielders
roles.head: Wide with it. Closer without.
points: When we have the ball, use the space near the touchlines to help the team spread out.
Show a clear angle for a pass and be willing to run with the ball.
When the opposition have the ball, come closer to the middle and help your teammates.
roles.cue: Where is the ball, and who needs me?

roles.title: Striker
roles.head: Give us somewhere to play
points: Stay available ahead so we have somewhere to play forwards.
Sometimes show towards the ball to support 8 and the wide players.
At other times, threaten space behind the defenders to create room for teammates.
When the opposition build, help slow their options instead of chasing everyone.
roles.cue: Do we need a short pass or space ahead?

frames.caption: Both defenders come too close together. The goalkeeper has fewer clear passing angles.
frames.altSummary: GK has the ball. Defenders 3 and 2 have crowded close to the centre rather than offering two separated passes. The space outside them is not being used.

frames.caption: 3 and 2 split to offer safe passing angles. 8 stays available ahead. Look short if it is on.
frames.altSummary: GK has possession and both defenders split into the spaces either side. Number 8 remains between the lines to offer a possible next pass. Pass arrows show possible options, not compulsory passes.

frames.caption: 11 and 7 stretch the pitch. 8 offers a central passing option, with 9 ahead.
frames.altSummary: In possession: the two wide midfielders stand closer to the touchlines, the central midfielder is available in the middle and the striker gives the team depth.

frames.caption: 11 and 7 recover inside to help 8 protect the middle. The team stays connected.
frames.altSummary: Out of possession: 11 has moved in from the left touchline and 7 from the right, closer to number 8 in the centre. The two defenders remain behind them and the striker remains available higher up.

frames.caption: Both defenders chase the same player. Space opens behind them.
frames.altSummary: Two defenders have moved across to challenge the opposition player near our left touchline. A grey central gap opens in front of goal. This is a risk, not a movement to teach.

frames.caption: 3 can meet the ball. 2 protects the space behind, and 8 helps in the middle.
frames.altSummary: An opposition player carries the ball on our left. Defender 3 goes to meet them, defender 2 stays more central and deeper, and 8 offers cover ahead. Only the nearest defender is closing down.

frames.caption: The ball has changed hands. We have players ahead of it, so we need to recover together.
frames.altSummary: The opposition has taken possession in the middle of the pitch. Our wide players are still high and wide, while 8 is nearest to the ball. Two defenders and the goalkeeper remain behind.

frames.caption: 8 slows the next attack. 11 and 7 move back towards the middle while 3 and 2 protect our goal.
frames.altSummary: The opponent still has the ball near the middle. 8 is close enough to delay, both wide midfielders have come nearer the centre, and two defenders remain behind them so the team can recover together.

frames.caption: Look for the two defenders and a safe pass, but do not force it.
frames.altSummary: The goalkeeper has the ball and looks towards two separated defenders and the central midfielder as possible teammates to play to.

frames.caption: Stay ready and help teammates with short, calm information.
frames.altSummary: The goalkeeper stays between the goal and two defenders, who protect the central area. An opponent holds the ball further forward.

frames.caption: Open up to receive. Give your goalkeeper an option.
frames.altSummary: Two defenders stand apart and available for a goalkeeper to pass into wide defensive positions.

frames.caption: If one meets the ball, the other covers. Stay connected.
frames.altSummary: Defender 3 meets an opposition ball carrier on our left and defender 2 is deeper and nearer the centre, covering the space towards our goal.

frames.caption: Move into space where a teammate can see and pass to you.
frames.altSummary: The central midfielder 8 offers a position ahead of the two defenders with wide teammates on both sides and the striker further forward.

frames.caption: Help protect the middle and support the nearest defender.
frames.altSummary: Number 8 is central between an opposition attacker and our goalkeeper while two defenders hold their positions behind.

frames.caption: Make the pitch big. Give teammates somewhere to pass.
frames.altSummary: Our wide midfielders 11 and 7 occupy the outside channels, with number 8 central.

frames.caption: Get closer to the middle so you're ready to help.
frames.altSummary: Both wide midfielders move inside and deeper towards number 8 when the opposition gain possession.

frames.caption: Sometimes come towards the ball to help us connect.
frames.altSummary: Number 9 moves towards the midfield line to become a shorter pass for number 8, with the wide midfielders providing width.

frames.caption: Other times run into space beyond the defence to help teammates.
frames.altSummary: Number 9 runs higher behind a pair of opponents while number 8 stays available as a supporting passer.

review.title: When to choose 2-3-1
review.why: England Football illustrates the shape as one option, not its preferred or prescribed formation.
qs: Does this balance suit both U10 and U11? What are the clearest trade-offs against 3-2-1?
Against two high opponents, what is the simplest correction for two defenders, without adding rigid instructions?
Are our shirt numbers merely illustrative, not fixed developmental positions?

review.title: Starting with the goalkeeper
review.why: The retreat line, goalkeeper's decisions and children's technical level affect what is sensible.
qs: Does 'two options' encourage unnecessary short passing under pressure?
Are the two defenders' distances appropriate on 7v7 pitch proportions?
Does the script respect the retreat line without claiming a rule that isn't included in the example?

review.title: Wide when we have it, closer when we don't
review.why: The biggest coaching challenge identified in grassroots discussion is wide players understanding two phases.
qs: Do the two diagram positions and movement arrows communicate clear choices without fixing children to channels?
Could the defensive tuck-in overcompress the team or leave an obvious easy outside pass?
Should we teach the same cue for U10 and U11?

review.title: Pressing, covering and recovering
review.why: Illustrative two-defender situations are a coaching hypothesis, not a rule.
qs: Does the two-defender pair make sense against different opposition shapes?
Is the nearest-player delay instruction suitable for the age group?
Should the striker recover more or block a passing lane in our final sequence?

review.title: Official rules and developmental suitability
review.why: FA guidance states no heading, no offside, a retreat line, rolling substitutions and encouragement to rotate positions.
qs: Do the diagrams accidentally depend on offside or heading being allowed?
Does the issue encourage rotation and enough playing time, not permanently allocated roles?
Verify illustrative pitch markings against the current 7v7 mini-soccer specifications before production sign-off.

issue.intro: Moving from 5v5 to 7v7 means two more players and more decisions. The 2-3-1 gives us a starting picture: two defenders, three midfielders and a striker, supported by the goalkeeper. Four simple ideas help players play together, without locking anyone into a role.
issue.summary: A researched draft of the 7v7 2-3-1: starting shape, four practical principles, every player role and how the team plays together.
